## Comparability caveats first

**Alaska Air Group is not cleanly comparable to the other four.** Alaska closed its acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings on September 18, 2024, and "[t]he results of Hawaiian are included in the consolidated financial statements beginning September 18, 2024" [DOC-2]. Its FY2024 figures therefore blend a full year of standalone Alaska with roughly 3.5 months of Hawaiian, which contributed $869 million of revenue and a $113 million net loss [DOC-2]. Alaska's FY2024 cost ratios are thus a mixed-basis figure, not an organic run-rate, and they are depressed by a loss-making partial-period business.

The other four are directly comparable on timing: all figures are calendar-year (Jan 1 – Dec 31) FY2024 10-K data [DOC-1].

A second limitation: the source provides only two expense lines — aircraft fuel and salaries/wages/benefits — not total operating expense [DOC-1]. So "cost structure" can only be measured as (fuel + labor) as a share of revenue, cross-checked against operating margin.

## Fuel + labor as a percentage of revenue (FY2024)

| Airline | Fuel | Labor | Combined | Revenue | % of revenue | Operating margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Delta | $10,566M | $16,161M | $26,727M | $61,643M | **43.4%** | **9.7%** |
| United | $11,756M | $16,678M | $28,434M | $57,063M | 49.8% | 8.9% |
| American | $11,418M | $16,021M | $27,439M | $54,211M | 50.6% | 4.8% |
| Alaska* | $2,506M | $3,588M | $6,094M | $11,735M | 51.9% | 4.9% |
| Southwest | $5,812M | $12,240M | $18,052M | $27,483M | 65.7% | 1.2% |

All inputs from [DOC-1]. *Alaska = mixed basis per [DOC-2].

## Conclusion

Delta has the most efficient cost structure on both available measures. It converts the lowest share of revenue into fuel and labor (43.4% vs. 49.8% for United, 50.6% for American, and 65.7% for Southwest) [DOC-1], and it posts the highest operating margin at 9.7% on $5,995M of operating income against $61,643M of revenue [DOC-1]. Southwest is clearly the least efficient, with labor alone consuming $12,240M of $27,483M in revenue (44.5%) and operating income of just $321M [DOC-1]. Alaska's apparent 51.9% cost ratio and 4.9% margin should be treated as provisional given the Hawaiian consolidation [DOC-2].

ANSWER: Delta Air Lines — lowest combined fuel + labor cost at 43.4% of revenue ($26,727M of $61,643M) and the highest operating margin at 9.7%, versus United 49.8%/8.9%, American 50.6%/4.8%, Alaska 51.9%/4.9% (mixed basis due to the partial-year Hawaiian consolidation), and Southwest 65.7%/1.2%.
